**Setting up the distribution.** Let $p=0.3$ (Frank wins a game) and $q=0.7$. The match ends at game $N=21+m$, where $m\in\{0,\dots,20\}$ is the number of losing-player wins. The match ends with Frank winning with probability $\binom{20+m}{m}p^{21}q^m$, and with Joe winning with probability $\binom{20+m}{m}q^{21}p^m$. So

$$E[N]=\sum_{m=0}^{20}(21+m)\left[\binom{20+m}{m}p^{21}q^m+\binom{20+m}{m}q^{21}p^m\right]=21+E[m].$$

**Evaluating $E[m]$.** Using $m\binom{20+m}{m}=21\binom{20+m}{m-1}$ and reindexing, the Frank-winning part becomes

$$\sum_m m\binom{20+m}{m}p^{21}q^m=\frac{21q}{p}\,P\big(\mathrm{Bin}(41,p)\ge 22\big),$$

and similarly the Joe-winning part equals $\frac{21p}{q}\,P\big(\mathrm{Bin}(41,q)\ge 22\big)$. (I checked this general identity against the case "first to 2 wins," where it gives the correct $E[N]=2+2pq$.)

With $p=0.3$, $q=0.7$, $\frac{21q}{p}=49$ and $\frac{21p}{q}=9$. Let $Y\sim\mathrm{Bin}(41,0.3)$. Then

$$E[N]=21+49\,P(Y\ge 22)+9\,P(Y\le 19).$$

**Numerical values.**

- $P(Y=20)\approx 0.0052414$
- $P(Y=21)\approx 0.0022463$
- $P(Y=22)\approx 0.00087518$, and summing the tail gives $P(Y\ge 22)\approx 0.0013236$
- $P(Y\le 19)=1-P(Y\ge 20)=1-(0.0052414+0.0022463+0.0013236)\approx 0.9911887$

Therefore

$$E[N]\approx 21+49(0.0013236)+9(0.9911887)\approx 21+0.06486+8.92070\approx 29.986.$$

This is consistent with intuition: Frank's win rate of 30% means the loser typically wins about $21\cdot 0.3/0.7\approx 9$ games, so the match lasts about $21+9=30$ games.

The expected number of games per match is about 29.99.

ANSWER: $\approx 29.99$
